clue.text: Cruel boss east European journalist found by Danube?

parts.note: a Slav is a member of a people of eastern Europe
ED is short for editor, the crossword's stock journalist
the Danube is an example of a river, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A harsh employer from eastern Europe, a newspaperman, is discovered beside the Danube.
explanation.definitionFit: A slave-driver is an idiom for a harsh employer who works staff mercilessly.

clue.text: Lines around animal's coat? Only part of it

indicators.note: the lines wrap round the animal

parts.note: L stands for line, so two make lines
an ape is an animal

explanation.surface: Lines drawn around an animal's coat cover only part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded flap on the front of a jacket, one portion of it.

clue.text: Came to place with daughter after six

indicators.note: after puts the place-and-daughter pair following the number

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a site is a place

explanation.surface: Someone arrived somewhere with their daughter after six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came to' looks like regaining consciousness, but means called on.
explanation.definitionFit: Visited means called at or went to see a place.

clue.text: Infer bird has lost its tail in river

indicators.note: in places the shortened bird within the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: a word losing its tail drops its final letter

parts.note: a duck is a bird

explanation.surface: Work out that a waterbird has lost its tail feathers in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost its tail' drops the last letter of the bird. The Dee is a river in Wales and England, and another in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce is to conclude by reasoning, the same as infer.

clue.text: Omit meal possibly, making sacrifice

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Skipping lunch could be seen as a kind of personal sacrifice.
explanation.definitionFit: To immolate is to kill as an offering, especially by burning.

clue.text: Number one story for uplift and joy

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplift means the letters are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A top tale brings uplift and happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for uplift' turns the whole of NO + I + TALE, giving ELAT I ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness and exhilaration.

clue.text: Countrymen on public transport start to hit part of London

parts.note: shepherds are rural folk who tend flocks
a bus is public transport

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Rural folk riding a bus begin to make an impact on a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEPHERD'S BUSH is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Shepherd's Bush is a district of west London, an example of a city area.

clue.text: Faithful worker goes after jailbird on street

indicators.note: goes after means follows, so the worker comes last

parts.note: a con is a convict
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A loyal employee chases a convict down the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant means steadfast and loyal.

clue.text: Prison concert organised by Albert?

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A concert in a jail is arranged by someone called Albert.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert, husband of Queen Victoria, held the title Prince Consort; the question mark marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert of Saxe-Coburg was the royal husband given that title, so an example.

clue.text: Expectations the man's got outside work

indicators.note: the man's letters sit outside, wrapping round the word for work

parts.note: the man's is HE'S, short for he is or he has
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Hopes are what a fellow has when he has got a job outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopes are aspirations, things one anticipates or wishes for.

clue.text: A nude more naughty in general disposition

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are set wrongly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A naked person behaving even more cheekily reveals their character.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeanour is outward manner or bearing, a person's overall way of behaving.

clue.text: Getting into the party spirit?

parts.note: a phrase about joining the fun at a celebration, reread as becoming involved with a party in the sense of a governing faction

explanation.definitionFit: Political describes involvement with parties of government, so entering into a party's spirit is being partisan in that sense.

clue.text: On reflection Nesbit is deficient as writer

indicators.note: seen as in a mirror, the letters run backwards
deficient means lacking something, here the final letter of the name Nesbit

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, the children's author Nesbit falls short as a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deficient' cuts the T from NESBIT, leaving NESBI, and 'On reflection' turns that round. E. Nesbit wrote The Railway Children.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was a Norwegian playwright, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Animals in oriental countries

parts.note: E stands for east, so oriental gives the compass letter
lands is another word for nations or countries

explanation.surface: Creatures are found in the nations of the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Elands are large African antelopes, examples of animals.

clue.text: Having the freedom to choose a material involves skill

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so the fabric holds the skill

parts.note: lace is a fabric
art is skill

explanation.surface: Choosing freely, a fabric takes some craftsmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: À la carte describes ordering separately priced dishes off a menu, so with free selection.

clue.text: Salt from tin, say, girl's swallowed

indicators.note: the girl is taken inside, gulped down by the word for say

parts.note: to state is to say
Ann is a girl's name; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A girl has swallowed some sort of salt made from tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl's swallowed' reads as the girl is swallowed, so 's is 'is', not a possessive. 'Salt' is the chemical sense, not table salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A stannate is a chemical salt derived from tin, whose Latin name is stannum.

clue.text: Chemical broken down by sue, DPhil

indicators.note: broken down means taken apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemical substance is analysed by Sue, who has a doctorate.
explanation.walkthrough: A DPhil is an Oxford doctorate.
explanation.definitionFit: A sulphide is a compound of sulphur, a chemical.

clue.text: Row in this way accommodates a plant

indicators.note: accommodates means makes room for, so the word for row holds the letter

parts.note: a din is a row in the sense of a loud noise
thus means in this manner

explanation.surface: An argument conducted like this makes room for some greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is a noise, not a line or a quarrel: DIN takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: Dianthus is a genus of flowering plants including pinks and carnations.

clue.text: Cherry perhaps gets chopped — a boy's crime?

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the tree loses its final letter

parts.note: a cherry is an example of a tree
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Chopping down a cherry tree — is that a boy's crime?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the tale of young George Washington felling his father's cherry tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country.

clue.text: Flower almost dry inside? Should be soaked!

indicators.note: the word for dry goes within the shortened flower
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a bloom is a flower
TT means teetotal, and a dry person drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A flower almost dry at its heart needs a good watering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the flower's last letter. TT, for teetotal, is the standard crossword meaning of dry; the exclamation hints the drinker should be soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is slang for very drunk, as is soaked.

clue.text: Learner with little energy, one certain to get time off studies?

parts.note: L is for learner, as on British L-plates
E is the abbreviation for energy
I is the Roman numeral for one
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A student short of energy is sure of a break from studying.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time away from work or duties.

clue.text: Thief providing gang with computers etc.

parts.note: a band is a gang
IT is information technology, covering computers and the like

explanation.surface: A robber supplies a gang with computer equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber, especially one of an armed gang.

clue.text: Carriage seen in thicket

definitions.meaning: a horse-drawn vehicle, an old wagonette
a dense patch of bushes or bracken

explanation.surface: An old coach is spotted in the undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake was a horse-drawn wagon; a brake is also a clump of brushwood or scrub.

clue.text: Religious types see parish going wrong

indicators.note: going wrong signals the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Pious people watch the local parish heading astray.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees were a strict Jewish sect in Roman times, so devout people.

clue.text: System of morals belonging to racial group without name

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for name is removed

parts.note: ethnic means relating to a racial or cultural group

explanation.surface: A moral code is found in a community that has no name.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles guiding conduct.

clue.text: Final day — is one coming in nourished, no longer hungry?

parts.note: Saturday, abbreviated SAT, is the last day of the week

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the letter for one goes inside

parts.note: fed means given food
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: On the last day, someone arrives fed and is hungry no more.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfied means sated, having eaten enough.

clue.text: Guide taking you and me to that woman

parts.note: us is the pronoun for you and me together
her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: A tour leader brings two of us along to see a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher is someone who shows people to their seats, so leads them.

clue.text: Lifelessness in piece of writing independent included

indicators.note: included means taken inside, so the letter goes within the written piece

parts.note: a sentence is a short piece of writing

explanation.surface: A lack of vitality shows in some writing containing an independent view.
explanation.definitionFit: Insentience is the state of lacking feeling or consciousness, as inert matter does.
